papers.title: Predicting county-level opioid overdose mortality in Ohio through multimodal data: A spatiotemporal study using toxicology and EMS indicators, 2020-2024
papers.abstract: Background The opioid crisis is the leading driver of overdose mortality in the United States. While overdose deaths have decreased in recent years, the reporting lag in official overdose deaths presents a hurdle in implementing public health interventions to combat the crisis. Objective To address these data-reporting delays and improve prediction during highly volatile periods, we developed a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model using real-time drug overdose data sources to predict quarterly overdose deaths across Ohio counties from 2020 to 2024. Methods We implemented a Bayesian spatiotemporal model using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA). Rapid-reporting surveillance metrics, specifically urine drug test (UDT) positivity rates and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) naloxone administration events, were incorporated as fixed covariates. Models were constructed stepwise by first optimizing the spatiotemporal random effect structure and then sequentially adding fixed effects to minimize prediction error. A rolling training window was implemented and evaluated across different training window sizes. Results were assessed overall and stratified by county population size. Results We found that the optimal predictive model structure consists of a two-year training window, a random walk temporal effect, a structured spatial effect, and fentanyl UDT positivity and EMS naloxone events. Incorporating these UDT and EMS data significantly enhanced predictive performance, with the most pronounced accuracy gains occurring during the unprecedented overdose increase associated with the COVID-19 pandemic in the second quarter of 2020. While predictive performance was highly robust in large, urban counties, predictive capability in smaller counties was limited by low data availability. Conclusion Our spatiotemporal prediction model successfully bridges the administrative reporting lags and offers near-real-time quarterly overdose prediction. The study also showed that integration of real-time data sources is especially beneficial for capturing sudden, volatile spikes in overdose deaths.

papers.title: Unmet needs of Polish patients with cystic fibrosis seen through the lens of crowdfunding
papers.abstract: Medical crowdfunding allows for funding for needs not covered by the local healthcare system. We aimed to characterize the crowdfunding campaigns for the needs of Polish individuals with cystic fibrosis (CF). In our study, we analyzed data from a leading medical crowdfunding webpage in Poland, focusing on campaigns for individual medical needs initiated between 2009 and 2017. We characterized the features of individuals with CF and the declared goals for which the funds from the online campaigns were intended. Of all 2,656 campaigns, 96 (3.6%) were related to individuals with CF. Approximately two-thirds of these campaigns reached their target amount. Individuals with CF primarily raised funds to cover treatment costs, medical equipment, and entertainment. The successful collection had a significantly lower financial target than unsuccessful campaigns. If the receivers were living in a city or fundraising to gather funds for an inhaler, these were also associated with the campaign's success. However, these associations were slightly above the threshold of statistical significance. Crowdfunding campaigns can be an effective funding source for the needs of patients with CF that are not covered by the public healthcare system. Analyzing crowdfunding efforts for specific patient groups can help reveal their unmet health needs.

papers.title: Changes in Health Behaviors and Correlational Patterns among High School Students Across Two Longitudinal Studies
papers.abstract: Purpose - This study examines whether six health behaviors remain stable among high school students across the school year and whether associations between these behaviors recur across assessments. Design/methodology/approach - As part of a school health program evaluation, a pre-post longitudinal health survey was conducted among two samples of high school students in a U.S. vocational-technical high school. Study 1 surveyed 114 students from late winter to late spring in 2024. Study 2 surveyed 177 students from autumn 2024 to late spring 2025. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests examined group-level behavioral change, and Pearson correlation networks described associations among six health behaviors: sleep, breakfast consumption, physical activity, nature exposure, social media use, and mindfulness practices. Findings - The primary analyses detected no significant group-level changes in any of the six behaviors across either study interval, suggesting relative stability within these samples. A one-time survey may provide useful information for broad school health planning, whereas repeated assessment remains necessary for evaluating longer-term patterns or program effects. Sleep and breakfast showed the most consistent positive association. Physical activity and nature exposure were positively associated at three of the four assessments. Social media was isolated from the other behaviors at the first three assessments but was negatively associated with sleep and physical activity at the final assessment. Originality - The study distinguishes stability in group-level behavior from changes in the relationships among behaviors. The findings support efficient assessment for broad educational planning. They also identify behavior pairs that can be addressed together in school health education, including sleep and breakfast, physical activity and nature exposure, and social media, sleep, and physical activity.

papers.title: Stigma and unsupportive disclosure reactions are associated with elevated depressive symptom burden among adolescent mothers in Juja Sub-County, Kenya: a community-based cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Girls who become pregnant during adolescence in sub-Saharan Africa carry a high burden of depressive symptoms. Kenyan studies have relied on antenatal clinic samples and have not looked at stigma, the response to pregnancy disclosure and economic circumstances in the same analysis. We assessed how these factors relate to depressive symptom burden among adolescent mothers in Juja Sub-County, Kiambu County. We surveyed 227 girls who had been pregnant or given birth at 10-19 years, drawn by stratified random sampling from a line list of 466 mapped across five wards. Trained assistants administered a structured questionnaire covering background characteristics, pregnancy and disclosure, stigma, and a seven-item depressive symptom checklist. Elevated symptom burden was set in advance at four or more endorsed items. Two logistic regression models examined factors linked to stigma (n = 199) and to elevated symptom burden (n = 184). Of those with parity data, 194 of 197 had already given birth. Most respondents were 17-19 years old (86.8%) and single (69.2%), 92.5% had no income of their own, and 47.1% had left school early. Nine in ten pregnancies (91.2%) were unplanned, and 41.4% of girls met anger, rejection or indifference when they first disclosed. Stigma was reported by 43.2%, elevated symptom burden by 27.1% and thoughts of self-harm by 16.4%. Only 27.3% had attended any support programme. Being single was the one factor associated with stigma (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 3.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.48-8.31). Elevated symptom burden was associated with stigma (AOR 3.21; 1.54-6.69) and with an unsupportive disclosure reaction (AOR 2.54; 1.19-5.41), and was less likely with each additional year of age (AOR 0.69; 0.49-0.96). Programme attendance showed no association (AOR 0.89; 0.41-1.94). In this peri-urban community, depressive symptoms clustered among adolescent mothers who had been stigmatised or poorly received when they disclosed their pregnancy, and stigma tracked marital status more closely than poverty. Screening with validated tools at postnatal, child-health and antenatal visits, guidance for families and partners on responding to disclosure, and community work on attitudes to unmarried motherhood deserve testing in this setting.

papers.title: Young peoples experiences of green social prescribing at a community farm and perceived influences on mental health and wellbeing: a qualitative study in Wales
papers.abstract: Mental health difficulties often begin in adolescence and early adulthood, yet most evidence on green social prescribing, which connects people with nature-based community activities to support health and wellbeing, comes from adult and quantitative research. This qualitative study explored how young people experienced taking part in a community farm programme in Wales and how they felt it influenced their mental health and wellbeing. Twelve young people aged 16 to 25 years took part in individual, semi-structured interviews at Swansea Community Farm in 2026. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis within an interpretivist paradigm. Four interconnected themes were developed: belonging in a supportive community; finding purpose through meaningful participation; personal growth and enhanced wellbeing; and nature as the context for wellbeing. Participants rarely described nature alone as responsible for feeling better. Instead, the farm brought together people who accepted them, useful work with real responsibility, and time outdoors with animals, and these were experienced together rather than separately. Participants had found the farm informally, and none had been referred through a formal social prescribing pathway. These findings suggest that green social prescribing for young people may work best when it is designed around belonging, meaningful roles and responsibility, with nature as the setting that makes these possible, and that evaluation should capture belonging, confidence and purpose as well as symptom reduction. They also point to the need for clear, youth-friendly routes into community provision, including self-referral. This was a single-site study, so it cannot show causal effects or represent the experiences of young people who did not engage, but it offers an in-depth account to inform the design and evaluation of provision for young people

papers.title: Ni Binti Ni Mama: Participatory, human-centred development of a targeted nurturing care model for teenage mothers and their children in Kakamega County, Kenya - a mixed-methods study
papers.abstract: Teenage mothers and their children face multiple barriers to nurturing care, yet few models translate the Nurturing Care Frameworks targeted support level into practice for this group in sub-Saharan Africa. We describe the participatory, human-centred development of Ni Binti Ni Mama ( she is a girl, she is a mother), a targeted nurturing care model for teenage mothers in Kakamega County, Kenya. In phase one, a needs assessment combined a structured questionnaire and observation checklist covering the five nurturing care components (57 teenage mothers of infants), in-depth interviews with five mothers and five key informant interviews with health workers. Component scores were compared across groups using Welchs t-tests; qualitative data were analysed thematically. In phase two, a stakeholder workshop with the sub-county health management team and university experts generated and prioritised strategies; a draft community health volunteer training module was tried out with 21 volunteers. The mean overall nurturing care score was 69.1% (SD 10.3). Uptake of maternal and child health services was high (good health score 88.1%), whereas early learning scored lowest (40.4%): 28.1% of children had a picture book and 15.8% of mothers had read or looked at pictures with their child the previous day. Most mothers (75.4%) had skipped meals for lack of money. Responsive caregiving was lower among mothers reporting emotional stress (76.4% vs 86.0%; p=0.005). Interviews described economic dependence, absent fathers, family conflict, peer stigma and food insecurity. The resulting model, framed by Social Cognitive Theory, combines community health volunteer home visits, school and family sensitisation, teen mothers clubs and peer mentorship, lactation support for school re-entry, and linkage to youth-friendly services and economic support. Teenage mothers informed the model through their needs and preferences but did not participate in design decisions; their direct involvement and a feasibility evaluation are the next steps.

papers.title: Determinants of Tuberculosis Diagnosis Delays among Patients Attending Public Health Facility of Metekel Zone, Northwest Ethiopia, 2024 unmatched Case-Control Study
papers.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis Diagnosis delays among tuberculosis patients can worsen infection transmission, disease severity, and mortality risk. Identifying factors influencing delays is crucial due to its persistence across healthcare levels and communities. The study identify determinants of tuberculosis diagnosis delay among patients attending public health facility of Metekel zone, Northwest Ethiopia:2023 Methods: An unmatched case-control study was conducted in Metekel zone health facilities from March to April 2023, involving 210 tuberculosis patients (103 cases, 107 controls) selected through systematic sampling. Data collected through structured questionnaires and STATA used for analysis, including bi-variable and multi-variable logistic regressions. Variables with p-value < 0.25 in bi-variable analysis were included in the final model after checking model fitness and multicollinearity. Results: Overall, 210 tuberculosis patients were included in the study. The following independent variables were associated diagnosis delay of tuberculosis: TB patients who travel greater than 10km (AOR: 2.941, (95 % CI: 1.509, 5.731); TB patients who are living at rural area (AOR: 4.135, 95 % CI :1.759, 9.723); TB patients who prior visit in holly-water and traditional medicine [AOR: 2.978, (95% CI: 1.292, 6.863); poor knowledge about TB [AOR: 2.826, (95% CI: 1.404, 5.687)]. Conclusion: Tuberculosis diagnosis delay is a major challenge to eliminate tuberculosis by breaking the chain of transmission. This study can be attributed to factors including place of residence being rural, poor knowledge about tuberculosis, non-health facility initial actions upon symptom onset, and far distance to health institutions. Recognizing these determinants helps in identifying and addressing barriers inhibiting early diagnosis, potentially improving healthcare access and promoting more timely diagnosis and treatment for tuberculosis patients.

papers.title: Long-term cooking fuel use patterns following a clean cooking intervention: Follow-up of the multi-country HAPIN trial
papers.abstract: Introduction: The exposure and health benefits of clean cooking depend on sustained, exclusive use, yet few studies have assessed fuel use after trial support ends. We conducted a prospective follow-up of the Household Air Pollution Intervention Network (HAPIN) trial cohort to assess cooking fuel use for 4 years post-trial in India, Guatemala, and Rwanda. Methods: Intervention households in the HAPIN trial received a free liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) stove, fuel, and behavioral support for 18 months. At trial completion, control participants in Guatemala and Rwanda were offered a free LPG stove or alternative compensation, and in India, a free LPG stove and 18 months of free fuel. We surveyed 2,169 participants annually for four years on exclusive and any LPG use, examined post-trial use trajectories, and assessed factors associated with post-trial LPG use using logistic regression. Results: Despite near-exclusive use during the trial, post-trial, few intervention participants used LPG exclusively (29% in India, <3% in Guatemala, near 0% in Rwanda). By year 4, 82% (India), 50% (Guatemala), and 10% (Rwanda) of intervention participants used any LPG. Sustained use was highest in India; non-use was most common in Rwanda; delayed use (starting years 3-4) was most common in Guatemala. Intervention assignment (aOR 1.8 [1.3-2.7], driven by Guatemala), socioeconomic status (up to aOR 40.9 [15.7-106.6] for Q4, relative to Q1), perceived ability to use LPG (aOR 3.9 [2.6-5.7]), household size (aOR 0.86 [0.79-0.93] per member), and country (aOR 5.4 [2.3-12.5] for India; aOR 1.9 [1.3-2.7] for Guatemala, relative to Rwanda) were significantly associated with post-trial LPG use. Only 27% of Guatemalan and 7% of Rwandan control participants chose an LPG stove (or electric, in Guatemala) as compensation, citing unaffordability and inaccessibility. Conclusions: A time-limited intervention, though successful in promoting LPG preference and sustained non-exclusive use in India and Guatemala, is unlikely to sustain the exclusive clean fuel use needed for long-term environmental and health benefits without policies supporting affordability and accessibility.

papers.title: Intimate partner violence victimization and perpetration with greater probability of brain injury in victims: A preliminary study
papers.abstract: Background: Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) can be either unidirectional or bidirectional. At times when it is bidirectional, the impact of the IPV would likely be greater in women compared to men especially in cases involving physical IPV. This study compared IPV victimization and perpetration characteristics and explored the relationship between IPV victimization and brain injury (BI) among women victims of IPV. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 23 women (IPV victims) aged 18-60 years who experienced at least one reported incident of IPV-BI were recruited from different community-based, women-serving organizations. Data collection included a comprehensive assessment of IPV, BI, and psychopathological comorbidities. The Conflict Tactics Scale-2 (CTS2) was used to assess for victimization and perpetration. Results: The participants had significantly lower scores on the physical assaults (t = 5.94, p < 0.0001, p2 = 0.62), and higher scores on the injury (t = 6.12, p < 0.001, p2 = 0.63) domains of the CTS2 compared to the perpetrator/partner. The physical assault scores of the perpetrator/partner were significantly correlated with the injury scores of the victim (r = 0.86, p < 0.001). Moreover, victims injury scores and their BISA scores were also significantly correlated (r = 0.69, p = 0.002). Conclusions: Women victims of IPV, in contrast to perpetrator/partners, demonstrated greater physical injury, which were associated with an increased likelihood of BI in this cohort. Findings should be interpreted cautiously, as partners data were based on victim reports. Further studies are warranted to explore the possible occurrence of BI in perpetrators and then directly compare the injury exposure in victims versus perpetrators. Based on the findings of this study, it is clear there is a higher prevalence, as well as greater exposure, of BI and more serious consequences of IPV and/or IPV-BI on victims compared to that of perpetrators.

papers.title: Validity and reliability of the SSF Preschoolers' Activity Questionnaire (SSF-PAQ) for assessing active play, screen time, and sleep in Japanese preschool children
papers.abstract: Background: The parent-reported Sasakawa Sports Foundation Preschoolers' Activity Questionnaire (SSF-PAQ) is from a national survey of Japanese preschoolers' out-of-preschool exercise, active play, screen time, and sleep. We assessed the validity, reliability, measurement error, paper-electronic agreement, and practicality of the Original version and explored a 24-hour version (SSF-PAQ-24). Methods: Children aged 3-6 years from 10 conveniently sampled preschools wore an accelerometer for seven days while parents kept a time-use diary and completed the SSF-PAQ on Days 7 and 10. Criteria were accelerometer-measured physical activity (PA), diary-recorded screen time, and diary- and accelerometer-derived night sleep. Results: The concurrent-validity sample comprised 167 children (Original, 127; SSF-PAQ-24, 40). Original-version correlations were weak for organized PA and active play ({rho} = 0.24) and moderate-to-vigorous PA ({rho} = 0.29) but strong for screen time ({rho} = 0.83) and night sleep ({rho} = 0.78), which averaged 8.2 and 10.7 min/day above the criteria. Test-retest intraclass correlations were 0.78-0.96 for these measures and 0.27-0.89 for setting-specific items. Screen time was higher on paper than electronically. SSF-PAQ-24 activity correlations were not significant ({rho} = 0.17 and 0.06). Completion took 6.5-9.7 minutes. Conclusion: The Original SSF-PAQ's main measures showed good-to-excellent test-retest reliability, and screen time and night sleep correlated strongly with the criteria. Activity-time validity was limited but comparable to that of existing parent-report questionnaires. SSF-PAQ-24 activity items need re-examination in a larger sample.

papers.title: Knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding antibiotic use and antimicrobial resistance among community pharmacy workers in Bukavu, Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: BackgroundCommunity pharmacies are often the first point of care in low- and middle-income countries, yet the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) of their workers regarding antibiotics and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) are undocumented in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). ObjectivesTo assess KAP regarding antibiotic use and AMR, and their determinants, among community pharmacy workers in Bukavu, Eastern DRC. MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted in April-June 2026 among 423 community pharmacy workers, one per pharmacy, selected by multistage sampling across the three health zones of Bukavu, using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire. Knowledge (8 items), attitudes (9 items) and dispensing practices (4 items) were scored using modified Blooms cut-offs. Multivariable logistic regression identified determinants. ResultsGood knowledge was found in 19.4%, favourable attitudes in 17.5% and appropriate dispensing practices in 27.4%. Overall, 96.5% dispensed antibiotics without a prescription and 9.2% knew the WHO AWaRe classification. University education and pharmaceutical qualification were independently associated with good knowledge [adjusted OR (aOR) 4.38 and 2.41] and appropriate practices (aOR 5.74 and 2.01). Good knowledge was associated with favourable attitudes (aOR 4.86, 95% CI 2.68-8.82), which in turn predicted appropriate practices (aOR 6.62, 95% CI 3.50-12.53). In addition, 57.0% knew of "Machange", an informal mixture of medicines: 99.6% of those describing its composition listed at least one antibiotic, and 65.6% of those familiar with it sold it. ConclusionsCommunity pharmacy workers in Bukavu show substantial gaps in antibiotic-related KAP. Stewardship interventions should combine education with regulation, diagnostic capacity and AMR surveillance within a One Health framework.

papers.title: Evaluation of a Study Advisory Group on the Facilitators and Barriers to Patient Engagement
papers.abstract: The facilitators and barriers to patient engagement in an advisory group (AG) were evaluated. The AG was formed to provide the "patient" voice in the development of a pragmatic trial to study multinutrient treatment in children with ADHD. The AG consisted of patient partners (those with lived experience and caregivers) and healthcare professionals (those working with children with ADHD). Eleven AG members completed the Patient Engagement in Research Scale, and five members participated in semi-structured interviews. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically, and five themes were identified. Together with the quantitative findings, key facilitators of engagement included flexible engagement, a sense of trust among AG members and the research team, and meaningful opportunities to contribute. Barriers included irregular communication from the research team, ambiguity regarding members roles, and underutilization of members competencies. Findings highlight the importance of interpersonal relationships and team dynamics and informed improvements such as more regular communication, improved onboarding processes to strengthen role clarity, and better leveraging of members expertise to support full engagement. This evaluation provides insights into the use of research evaluation to strengthen patient engagement in applied research settings.

papers.title: Under-perception of overweight, not genetic risk, tracks weight-loss goal-setting in a direct-to-consumer genetics cohort
papers.abstract: Services that rely on people to recognise their own weight and set their own goals may miss those who do not see themselves as overweight. We examined how adults perceive their weight, whether genetic risk of obesity, measured body size or early weight history explains who under-perceives it, and how perception relates to the weight-management goal they set, in a direct-to-consumer genetics cohort that includes people who have not sought care for their weight (FitnessGenes; N = 20,617). Although 61% of participants were overweight or obese by BMI, only 37% described themselves as such; among those overweight or obese by BMI, 64.0% placed themselves in a lighter category than their BMI indicated. Under-perception was more common in men than in women (73.5% vs 51.6%), in younger adults and at lower BMI, and a sex difference in the same direction, though smaller, was present when non-recognition of overweight was assessed against waist-to-height ratio rather than BMI. FTO rs9939609 behaved as an obesity risk variant (+0.46 kg/m{superscript 2} BMI and OR 1.18 for recalled childhood obesity per risk allele) but did not predict under-perception at a given BMI (per-allele OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.92-1.03), and neither did MC4R rs17782313 nor a combined score. A recalled history of childhood obesity, by contrast, was associated with heavier self-perception at the same adult BMI (+10.0 percentage points). At the same BMI, participants who under-perceived their weight were about half as likely to set a weight-loss goal (26.8% vs 47.5%; OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.48-0.56); among those obese by BMI, 49% who recognised it chose weight loss, against 18% who did not. Genotype did not predict goal- setting beyond its effect on BMI. Men were less likely both to recognise overweight and, having recognised it, to choose weight loss. Genetic risk of obesity therefore identifies who is likely to be heavier but not who will recognise it, and self-perception marks a group, mainly men and those at lower BMI, whom self-directed weight-management services are likely to under-reach.

papers.title: Sex and Gender Reporting and Female Participation Relative to Disease Burden in ClinicalTrials.gov
papers.abstract: ImportanceAssessing representation by sex assigned at birth and gender identity requires reporting of both in trials. If disclosure of full gender and sex participation from clinicaltrials.gov this is limited, it poses challenges in characterization and understanding of those participant experiences. ObjectiveTo determine how often ClinicalTrials.gov trials published trials report sex and gender, which characteristics are associated with reporting, and how participants female share compares with that of the general public. Design, Setting, and ParticipantsCross-sectional study of interventional trials registered to ClinicalTrials.gov, with or without US sites, with primary completion on or after September 27, 2008, and results first posted from January 1, 2009, through April 30, 2026. ExposuresFunder type, phase, US sites, enrollment, primary completion year, number of countries, and therapeutic area. Main Outcomes and MeasuresReporting of sex and gender, and the female participation-to-prevalence ratio (PPR; trial female share divided by the number of people with the condition). ResultsAmong 58,007 trials (median enrollment, 72 [IQR, 31 to 206]; 42,644 [74%] with US sites), 553 (0.95%) reported gender and 57,683 (99.44%) reported sex. Gender reporting was more common with National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding (odds ratio [OR], 9.05; 95% CI, 6.65 to 12.6), US sites (OR, 4.21; 95% CI, 2.96 to 6.22), and larger enrollment. Across 10 conditions (15,552 mixed-sex trials), median PPR ranged from 0.68 (95% CI, 0.64 to 0.71) for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease to 1.05 (95% CI, 1.01 to 1.09) for obesity and had a relatively lower female share in 8. Among the 10 conditions most prevalent in our cohort, 6,917 of 16,097 trial condition combinations (43.0%) reached a PPR of at least 0.90; odds of reaching it were higher for NIH-funded (OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.11 to 1.34) and lower for government-funded trials (OR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.20 to 0.33) as compared to industry-funded trials. Conclusions and RelevanceIn ClinicalTrials.gov, sex reporting is nearly universal, whereas gender reporting is concentrated among NIH-funded, US-based, and larger trials. Female trial enrollment fell below the female share of people with the condition for most conditions, emphasizing the benefit of condition-specific benchmarks in clinical trials.

papers.title: Wastewater metagenomic sequencing quantitatively tracks transmission dynamics for human pathogenic viruses
papers.abstract: Wastewater metagenomic sequencing theoretically characterizes all nucleic acids in a sample, but whether sequencing reads reflect transmission dynamics of circulating viruses in the contributing community is unknown. We evaluated if wastewater metagenomic sequencing data can be used to reconstruct transmission dynamics of endemic, routinely circulating viruses. Using deep, untargeted wastewater metagenomic sequencing data from four locations in the United States, we generated quantitative estimates of transmission dynamics (time-varying growth rate and effective reproduction number) within a Bayesian framework for widely monitored viruses. Across locations and viruses, estimates were statistically concordant with those derived from clinical surveillance and polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based wastewater monitoring data. Furthermore, we estimated growth rate from wastewater metagenomic sequencing data for numerous viruses not otherwise widely monitored, demonstrating the data expands the targets that can feasibly be monitored in parallel. Wastewater metagenomic sequencing can support both novel pathogen detection and routine surveillance of endemic pathogens.

papers.title: Chatbot as an intervention on physical activity: A systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression
papers.abstract: BackgroundChatbots offer scalable, accessible, and personalized support for physical activity (PA). This review synthesized evidence on their efficacy and examined potential moderators. MethodsEleven databases were searched for English-language published through January 27, 2026. Eligibility was assessed using the PICOS framework. Data extraction was guided by research questions, mERA checklist, and PRISMA 2020. Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and the NIH Quality Assessment Tool. Meta-analyses reported Hedges g. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Eggers regression, and trim-and-fill analyses. Potential moderators were examined through subgroup analyses and meta-regression. ResultsA total of 12,481 records were identified, of which 43 studies were included in the systematic review and 27 in the meta-analysis. Most studies included in the meta-analysis had some risk-of-bias concerns (16/27). Chatbot interventions produced a significant small-to-moderate post-intervention effect on PA (g = 0.31, 95% CI [0.19, 0.44]; n = 24), whereas the follow-up effect was small and non-significant (g = 0.11, 95% CI [-0.01, 0.22]; n = 4). Effects varied across PA outcomes (g = 0.08-0.44), and several subgroup differences helped explain the significant heterogeneity. For daily steps, significant subgroup differences were observed by clinical status, while intervention duration (QM = 6.09, p = 0.048) and clinical status (QM = 5.69, p = 0.017) were significant moderators. ConclusionsChatbot interventions showed small-to-moderate post-intervention effects but limited follow-up effects. Few significant moderators were identified, underscoring the need for more rigorous RCTs.

papers.title: Four waves of cancer-related risk behaviour and personal network data from a rural Romanian community
papers.abstract: 4P-CAN is an EU-funded project that collected longitudinal personal network data to investigate how cancer-related risk behaviours are socially organised within a rural community. Respondents (egos) describe the people they know (alters), their relationships with them, and relationships among alters. We share four waves of data collected between September 2023 and September 2025 in a Romanian rural community through interviewer-assisted network interviews and link-tracing recruitment. Five linked data tables contain 353 interviews with 142 adults, 7,602 alter roster entries identifying 2,480 people, 41,354 records of ego-reported acquaintance between alters, and recruitment-node and referral records. Linking individuals across networks and waves supports investigation of how cancer-related risk behaviours are distributed and clustered across community relationships. It also supports research on network composition, overlapping networks, reported health attributes and longitudinal measurement. Reuse should account for non-probability recruitment, dependence among observations and changes in measurement across waves.

papers.title: Unboxing unhealthy food marketing: An analysis of the extent and nature of unhealthy food marketing to children on YouTube in Canada using the CHOPPED artificial intelligence system
papers.abstract: BackgroundUnhealthy food marketing negatively affects childrens dietary patterns. However, little is known about the extent and nature of unhealthy food marketing to children on YouTube due to reliance on manual assessment methods. ObjectivesTo use a novel artificial intelligence (AI) system (CHild Oriented food Product Promotion Evaluation and Detection system, CHOPPED) to examine the extent and nature of unhealthy food marketing in YouTube videos suggested to Avatar accounts created for children and adults based on age and gender. MethodsOver two months of continuous monitoring, CHOPPED collected marketing instances played before, during, and after videos suggested by YouTubes algorithm to six child and two adult accounts that were not signed in and differed by age (2-4, 5-8, 9-12, [≥]18 years) and gender across four Canadian cities (Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, Halifax). CHOPPED characterized the extent and nature of monthly child-targeted unhealthy food marketing instances during 24-hour and typical 2-hour daily viewing periods. ResultsCHOPPED collected 60,633 marketing instances. No food marketing was shown to child accounts 2-4 years. On average, child accounts (5-12 years) were shown 25 monthly unhealthy food marketing instances during a 2-hour daily viewing period, 24 of which were child-targeted. The boys account (9-12 years) was shown a significantly higher monthly frequency of child-targeted unhealthy food marketing instances (340, 70.2%) than the boys account (5-8 years; 241, 66.2%), the girls account (5-8 years; 261, 60.6%), the mans account (224, 57.7%), and the womans account (263, 54.7%) during a 24-hour (p<0.05) but not a 2-hour daily viewing period. Monthly frequencies of some core child-targeted techniques shown to the boys account (9-12 years) were also higher than other accounts during a 24-hour (p<0.05) but not a 2-hour daily viewing period. ConclusionsThis study pioneered AI-driven analysis of the extent and nature of unhealthy food marketing to children on YouTube. Childrens potential exposure to such marketing on YouTube may be low. There was some evidence that the older boys account was shown more monthly child-targeted unhealthy food marketing instances and of some core child-targeted techniques than other accounts. On YouTube, food marketing may target a general audience rather than children by age and gender.

papers.title: Cardiovascular and metabolic trajectories in men engaged in a multidimensional preventive care program: a prospective observational study
papers.abstract: ObjectivesTo describe within-individual changes in cardiometabolic, functional and neuroendocrine markers between two standardized evaluations in men engaged in a structured preventive care program, and to examine transitions across clinical risk categories. DesignProspective observational cohort study using routinely collected data; paired within-individual analyses. SettingSingle preventive health center in Paris, France, offering a standardized multidisciplinary assessment with individualized lifestyle, supplementation and, when indicated, pharmacological recommendations. Participants279 men aged 18 years or older with a first evaluation (CU1) between October 2022 and November 2025 and a second evaluation (CU2) by May 2026 (32.3% of 865 eligible men); median interval 13.3 months (IQR 12.0-15.6). No exclusion criteria were applied. Primary and secondary outcome measuresWithin-individual change in continuous markers (Hodges- Lehmann estimate, 95% CI; Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment over 36 tests) and transitions across fixed clinical thresholds (paired odds ratios). ResultsMedian age was 51.2 years, BMI 24.5 kg/m{superscript 2} and SCORE2 2.9%. Visceral adipose tissue mass decreased ({Delta} -49 g, 95% CI -80.5 to -18.5; q=0.006), with small decreases in body mass and fat mass. Handgrip strength increased (right +2.35 kg, 1.70 to 3.00; left +1.70 kg, 1.05 to 2.30; q<0.001). HDL cholesterol increased (+3.5 mg/dL, 2.5 to 4.5; q<0.001), with decreases in the triglyceride/HDL and total/HDL ratios. Blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, fasting glucose (after adjustment), insulin, HOMA-IR, SCORE2 and salivary cortisol and DHEA did not change. The proportion of men below the grip strength reference value decreased from 60.1% to 47.6% (paired OR 0.34, 0.19 to 0.61) and with HDL cholesterol [≤]46 mg/dL from 26.7% to 16.5% (OR 0.25, 0.12 to 0.54). ConclusionsIIn this selected, health-engaged population of men who completed both evaluations, changes in a favorable direction were observed for handgrip strength, HDL cholesterol and visceral adiposity, whereas blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, glycemic markers and SCORE2 were stable. Without a comparison group, these changes cannot be distinguished from regression to the mean, test-retest effects or secular trends. Strengths and limitations of this studyO_LIStandardized assessment protocol applied identically at both evaluations, combining clinical, laboratory, DEXA body composition, functional and salivary neuroendocrine measurements in the same individuals. C_LIO_LIPaired within-individual analyses of 36 markers in 279 men, reported as effect estimates with confidence intervals and a global false discovery rate adjustment, with sensitivity analyses by follow-up interval and calendar period and a comparison of returners with 586 eligible non-returners. C_LIO_LISingle-arm design without a comparison group: the observed changes cannot be distinguished from regression to the mean, test-retest effects, participation effects or secular trends. C_LIO_LIHighly selected population of urban, socioeconomically advantaged, health-engaged men, of whom 32% returned for a second evaluation, limiting generalizability to the general population and to high-risk groups. C_LIO_LIStandardized effect sizes were small for most markers, adherence to recommendations was not measured objectively, and the follow-up was short. C_LI

papers.title: Quasi-experimental evaluation of a social media campaign to promote HPV vaccination in Bauchi state, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in women in 26 countries, including in sub-Saharan African countries. Cervical and other cancer risks can be greatly reduced through timely HPV vaccination and early screening. But it continues to pose a significant public health challenge in LMICs such as Nigeria. This study reports on the implementation and evaluation of a pair of social media behavior change campaigns to increase HPV vaccination amongst girls ages 9-14 and reduce vaccine hesitancy amongst girls and their parents in Bauchi state, Nigeria. The primary objectives are to conduct a quasi-experimental evaluation of the social media campaign; to examine the effect of higher versus lower levels of campaign exposure on HPV vaccination and related outcomes; to determine whether the social media campaign followed its planned theory of change; and to identify which social media messages were most effective in promoting HPV vaccination. We implemented an HPV vaccination social media promotion campaign, using videos designed to encourage parents to vaccinate their daughters, at scale in Bauchi state on the Meta and TikTok social media platforms. We used a quasi-experimental design, a heavy-up approach, that experimentally manipulated the level of social media content delivered in Bauchi. We used the Virtual Lab platform, an open-source platform that uses social media to recruit participants using advertising and creates panels of respondents for data collection through an online survey, and also collected social media metrics including impressions and engagement. The campaign was effective in increasing HPV vaccination rates from 69% at baseline to 86% at endline over 2 campaign phases that spanned approximately 3 months. Based on GEE modeling, we found that higher levels of engagement with the campaign were associated with higher vaccination rates at midline and endline. Pro-vaccine attitudes and reduced vaccine hesitancy also predicted higher vaccination rates. Also, the campaign produced additional HPV vaccinations at low cost: Adjusted for campaign exposure cost of $0.81 per additional vaccination in campaign phase 1, $2.10 per vax in phase 2, and $2.40 for the total campaign period. Evidence from this study indicates that social media may be an effective strategy to promote HPV vaccination at low cost. Future rigorous trials using experimental methods are needed to further evaluate social media to promote HPV vaccination.

papers.title: Geospatial AI targeting of tuberculosis active case finding in Pune, India: a quasi-experimental evaluation
papers.abstract: BACKGROUNDActive case finding (ACF) in India screens large populations to find few cases. AI-NETRA predicts neighbourhood-level tuberculosis (TB) risk from routine notification data and generates field microplans. OBJECTIVETo compare the yield and efficiency of AI-guided and standard ACF, and frontline acceptability. DESIGNProspective quasi-experimental evaluation in four TB Units of Pune district, comparing two-week AI-guided sweeps (April to May 2026) with the routine campaign in the same units (December 2024 to January 2025). Primary endpoint: bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB per persons screened; secondary: all-forms yield, presumptive yield, referral precision, number needed to screen (NNS) and cost per case. Acceptability: 16 focus groups (n=100) and a survey of 101 ASHAs. RESULTSAI-guided teams screened 66,095 people and confirmed 10 pulmonary cases, against 9 among 177,322 in the standard campaign (rate ratio 2.98, 95% CI 1.09 to 8.29); NNS was 6,610 versus 19,702 and cost per case 66% lower. All-forms detection did not differ (15 versus 32; RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.63 to 2.39); the standard campaign had mobile X-ray. 96% of ASHAs reported finding the same presumptive cases while screening fewer people. CONCLUSIONGeospatial targeting raised confirmed yield per person and lowered NNS; total detection did not differ. A concurrent, like-for-like trial is warranted.

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT AND INTERNAL EVALUATION OF MODELS FOR PREDICTING PROLONGED HOSPITALISATION AMONG PATIENTS WITH SICKLE CELL DISEASE IN A PUBLIC UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL IN GHANA
papers.abstract: BackgroundProlonged hospitalisation is an important burden among patients with sickle cell disease (SCD), with implications for healthcare utilisation and patient and caregiver burden. Early prediction may support timely clinical and resource-management interventions. ObjectiveTo identify factors associated with prolonged hospitalisation among patients with SCD and compare the predictive performance of multivariable logistic regression with five supervised machine-learning algorithms. MethodsThis retrospective study included SCD inpatients aged [≥]16 years admitted to the University of Ghana Hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, support vector machine, and k-nearest neighbours models were developed using five-fold stratified cross-validation. Class weighting and SMOTE were applied within training folds. Model performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC, AUC-PR, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), F1 score, and balanced accuracy. ResultsAmong 872 patients, 137 (15.7%) experienced prolonged hospitalisation. Acute chest syndrome (aOR=4.28; 95% CI: 2.31-7.94), malaria (aOR=3.77; 95% CI: 2.11-6.74), pneumonia (aOR=3.45; 95% CI: 2.02-5.90), and anaemia (aOR=2.71; 95% CI: 1.13-6.51) were independently associated with prolonged hospitalisation, whereas higher haemoglobin was protective (aOR=0.86; 95% CI: 0.78-0.96). Logistic regression achieved the highest AUC-ROC (0.692), F1 score (0.418) and balanced accuracy (0.677), while random forest achieved the highest AUC-PR (0.375). KNN had the highest sensitivity (59.3%) and XGBoost the highest specificity (87.2%). AUC-ROC confidence intervals overlapped substantially across models. ConclusionInfection-related complications and anaemia were important predictors of prolonged hospitalisation, while higher haemoglobin was protective. ML models showed modest performance without clear superiority over logistic regression. Larger multicentre studies with external validation are warranted.

papers.title: Antibiotic receipt by respiratory symptom group and source of care among children under five in Bangladesh: repeated cross-sectional analyses of national surveys, 2019 and 2025
papers.abstract: BackgroundAntibiotic use for childhood respiratory illness is common in low-income and middle-income countries, but national surveys rarely separate symptom groups or care pathways. We estimated antibiotic receipt among children under five in Bangladesh by reported respiratory symptom group, source of care and household wealth. MethodsWe analysed the 2019 and 2025 Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys. We included 4,010 children with cough and difficult breathing in the previous two weeks (3,990 in regression models). We compared breathing difficulty from the chest (suspected pneumonia) with nose-only symptoms, and five reported sources of care. Survey-weighted modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs). We described where antibiotic-treated children sought care and estimated slope indices of inequality (SIIs) by wealth. ResultsIn 2025, 68.5% (95% CI 64.2 to 72.5) of children with suspected pneumonia received an antibiotic, as did 54.3% (51.3 to 57.2) of children with nose-only symptoms. In pooled analyses of both surveys, the adjusted PR for nose-only symptoms was 0.83 (0.78 to 0.89). Against public health care, the pooled adjusted PR was 0.98 (0.91 to 1.07) for pharmacy care without a medical facility. It was 0.24 (0.20 to 0.29) for no advice or treatment sought. Pharmacy care rose from 18.8% to 36.5% of children with cough and difficult breathing between 2019 and 2025. By 2025, it accounted for 43.7% of treated children with suspected pneumonia and 42.2% with nose-only symptoms. Across the pooled surveys, receipt for suspected pneumonia was higher in richer children (SII 12.5 percentage points, 1.0 to 24.0). Recorded amoxicillin receipt in suspected pneumonia was 17.7% (14.7 to 21.1) in 2025, with no clear wealth gradient. ConclusionsAntibiotic receipt was common in both symptom groups, and care contacts shifted towards pharmacies. Receipt and care seeking differed by wealth. Antibiotic receipt should be monitored alongside symptoms and care contacts. Stewardship should be evaluated in medical and pharmacy settings while protecting access to assessment and appropriate treatment. The surveys cannot determine whether individual courses were appropriate.

papers.title: Evaluating menstrual-friendly public bathrooms in Atlanta, Georgia: An audit of availability, accessibility, and resources
papers.abstract: Public toilets are essential urban infrastructure that enable people who menstruate to participate in public life with dignity and comfort. However, little is known about whether publicly accessible toilets adequately support menstrual health and hygiene, particularly in high-income urban settings where privately operated facilities often function as de facto public infrastructure. This study assessed the menstrual friendliness of publicly accessible toilets in Atlanta, Georgia. We also examined differences by funding source (i.e., government versus private) and neighborhood type. We conducted field-based audits of womens, gender-neutral, and family toilets across 15 areas. Using an adapted Menstrual Friendly Public Toilet framework, we evaluated six dimensions: cleanliness, privacy and safety, structural features, general resources, accessibility, and menstrual health and hygiene resources. We calculated domain-specific and overall scores and compared government- and privately funded facilities, with additional descriptive comparisons across business, residential, tourist, and transit neighborhoods. We audited 125 toilet facilities across 112 locations. The overall mean Menstrual Friendly Public Toilet Index was 0.797. Cleanliness (0.974), privacy and safety (0.954), structure (0.930), and general resources (0.899) scored relatively high, whereas accessibility (0.622) and menstrual health and hygiene resources (0.490) scored lowest. Only 4.0% of facilities provided menstrual products or a functional dispenser. Overall scores did not differ significantly by funding source, although government-funded facilities had higher structural feature scores than privately funded facilities (0.952 versus 0.913; p=0.027). Menstrual health and hygiene resource scores varied across neighborhood types, ranging from 0.200 in the residential area to 0.775 in the tourist area. These findings demonstrate that the availability of clean and functional bathrooms does not necessarily ensure people can fully meet and manage their menstrual needs. Addressing gaps in accessibility and menstrual-specific resources will require coordinated attention to both government- and privately managed facilities, as well as consideration of neighborhood context to support menstrual health and equitable participation in urban public spaces.

papers.title: Projecting Introduction Timelines for Cholera Conjugate Vaccine and Typhoid-Cholera Conjugate Combo Vaccine: A Scenario-Based Forecasting Approach
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to project introduction timing and pathways of cholera conjugate vaccine (CCV) and combined typhoid-cholera conjugate vaccines (TCV/CCVs) in 39 low- and middle-income countries and to assess potential barriers to their routine immunization integration. MethodsAccelerated failure time models were fitted using oral cholera vaccine (OCV) introduction as a proxy for CCV adoption. Country-level estimates were standardized using observed post-WHO-prequalification introduction intervals for analogous vaccine transitions. TCV/CCV introduction timing and pathways were projected by combining standardized CCV estimates with a TCV introduction priority index based on typhoid burden and previous vaccination experience. Potential barriers to routine immunization integration were assessed using semi-quantitative scoring approach. ResultsGavi, the Vaccine Alliance (Gavi) eligibility, greater previous OCV experience, and higher cholera intensity were associated with earlier introduction times. After standardization, the median projected time to CCV introduction was 6.9 years after WHO prequalification, with 12 countries introducing within five years. The TCV/CCV projections comprised three pathways: CCV introduction followed by transition to TCV/CCV, direct TCV/CCV introduction and continued CCV use without TCV/CCV introduction during the analysis period. Projected introduction timing was not consistently aligned with routine integration barrier levels for either vaccine. ConclusionsThese scenario-based projections provide an early indication of where and when demand may emerge and which countries may require additional programmatic or financing support. The findings can inform demand forecasting, market assessment, manufacturing and supply planning, investment decisions, and introduction preparedness, but the projections should be recalibrated as product-specific evidence becomes available.

papers.title: Generative AI Versus Primary Care Physicians from Plan Initiation to Long-Term Maintenance of Chronic Disease Self-Management: A Vignette-Based Validation Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundGenerative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may provide personalised and dynamically adjustable support for chronic disease self-management. However, previous studies have largely focused on isolated questions and a limited range of evaluation dimensions. ObjectiveTo compare the quality of self-management advice generated by GenAI and primary care physicians (PCPs) across multiple stages of chronic disease management and evaluation dimensions. MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional, source-blinded comparative evaluation using 15 standardised vignettes of diabetes and hypertension derived from authentic primary care follow-up records. Each vignette comprised three sequential management stages, with medical accuracy, readability, and behaviour-change potential assessed across the three simulated stages; individualisation and multidisciplinary integration at plan initiation; contextual adaptability during acute adjustment; and empathy during long-term maintenance. The GenAI system and 22 PCPs independently generated advice which was independently rated by three clinicians, one each from general practice, endocrinology, and cardiology. across seven dimensions. Linear mixed-effects models were used for the primary comparisons, and case-level paired and physician-distribution analyses were conducted as robustness analyses. ResultsThe GenAI system achieved estimated marginal means above 4.0 in all dimensions except readability. It scored significantly higher than PCPs in six of the seven dimensions, with adjusted mean differences ranging from 1.16 to 1.56 points (P<.001). Readability was the only exception, with no significant difference between GenAI and PCPs (-0.22, 95% CI -0.54 to 0.11; P=.19). The GenAI mean exceeded the individual means of all recruited PCPs in the six dimensions but ranked at approximately the 23rd percentile for readability. ConclusionsOur findings indicated the GenAI system may generate more highly rated self-management advice than PCPs across most evaluated dimensions but offered no advantage in readability. These findings provide pre-implementation evidence for GenAI as a potential source of structured and adaptive chronic disease self-management support. Patient-level pilot studies and subsequent randomised trials are needed to determine its acceptability and effects on behaviour and clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents in Sekondi-Takoradi, Western Region of Ghana: A community-based cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Mpox re-emerged as a global public health concern in 2022, and the Western Region of Ghana became the epicentre of the countrys largest recorded outbreak in 2025. Ahead of a sub-national vaccination campaign launched in October 2025, no study had examined the determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the region using a theoretically grounded framework. This study determined the sociodemographic and Health Belief Model-based determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolis, Western Region, Ghana. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 580 adults in six purposively selected peri-urban areas and their surrounding communities between July and August 2025, before the vaccination campaign began. Vaccine acceptance was measured as a three-category outcome (accept, hesitant, refuse) and analysed using chi-square tests and multinomial logistic regression adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, Health Belief Model constructs, and peri-urban area. Overall, 75.7% of respondents were willing to accept the vaccine, 12.9% were hesitant and 11.4% would refuse. Perceived vaccine safety was the strongest determinant: respondents who considered the vaccine very safe had markedly lower adjusted odds of hesitancy (adjusted odds ratio 0.02, 95% confidence interval 0.00-0.12) and refusal (0.03, 0.01-0.13) than those who considered it unsafe. Uncertainty about vaccine effectiveness was associated with hesitancy (9.83, 1.95-49.50), and belief in its effectiveness with lower odds of refusal (0.22, 0.06-0.86). Higher educational attainment was associated with lower odds of hesitancy, being a student or employed with lower odds of refusal, and acceptance differed between peri-urban areas (55.1% to 95.6%). Knowledge of mpox transmission was associated with acceptance in bivariate analysis (p < 0.001) but not after adjustment. Risk communication that addresses vaccine safety and effectiveness, rather than generic disease-awareness messaging alone, is likely to be most effective in improving mpox vaccine acceptance in this population, with unemployed and less-educated residents warranting targeting. As a pre-campaign baseline collected during an active outbreak, these findings can inform the vaccination response in the Western Region and preparedness in comparable peri-urban West African settings.

papers.title: Determinants of early child development among children aged 24-59 months in Ethiopia: 2024-25 Demographic and Health Survey
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe 2024-25 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) is the first national survey in Ethiopia to measure early childhood development using UNICEFs Early Childhood Development Index 2030 (ECDI2030). This provides a national estimate for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 4.2.1, the proportion of children aged 24-59 months who are developmentally on track. We estimated the prevalence of being developmentally on track and examined its child, maternal, household and community determinants in Ethiopia. MethodsThis cross-sectional study analysed 3,731 children aged 24-59 months (weighted n = 3,514) of 3,232 mothers in 771 clusters. Children were on track if they achieved the age-specific minimum number of the 20 ECDI2030 milestones. Prevalence was estimated with design-based methods. Four three-level mixed-effects logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) were fitted, and interviewer effects were assessed. ResultsOverall, 36.3% (95% CI 33.4-39.3) of children were developmentally on track. Prevalence ranged from 23.3% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 77.7% in Addis Ababa. In the null model, 21.5% of the variation lay between clusters (median odds ratio 3.24). In the final model, the odds of being on track were lower at 36-47 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 0.57, 95% CI 0.44-0.74) and 48-59 months (AOR 0.39, 0.30-0.51) than at 24-35 months. They were also lower after a preceding birth interval under 24 months (AOR 0.75, 0.57-0.99), after recent diarrhoea, fever or cough (AOR 0.59, 0.45-0.77), and where distance to a health facility was a big problem (AOR 0.61, 0.48-0.79). Odds were higher for girls (AOR 1.38, 1.12-1.70), with maternal education (more than secondary vs none: AOR 2.08, 1.19-3.63) and with weekly media exposure (AOR 2.15, 1.51-3.06). The covariates explained 55.9% of the between-cluster variance. ConclusionsNearly two in three Ethiopian children aged 24-59 months are not developmentally on track, and children fall further behind as they age. Interventions should target maternal education, access to information and health services, birth spacing and childhood illness, with priority for the lowest-performing regions and communities.

papers.title: Gender Differences in Socioeconomic Inequalities in Body Mass Index and Health-Related Mediators Among Young and Early Midlife Finns
papers.abstract: IntroductionSocioeconomic differences in body mass index (BMI) are well established, but less is known about gender differences and their behavioral pathways. We examined gender differences in the association between socioeconomic position (SEP) and BMI, and whether dietary factors and physical activity mediated the associations. MethodsWe used survey data from the employees of the City of Helsinki aged 19-39 collected in 2017 (n = 4,400, 80% women). SEP was measured by highest educational attainment, and the examined mediators were consumption of fruit and vegetables, red and processed meat, sweets and confectionery and alcohol as well as leisure-time vigorous physical activity (VPA) and sedentary time. We conducted gender-specific multiple mediation analyses using structural equation modeling and additional analyses using multiple imputation by chained equations. ResultsWith increasing educational attainment, mean BMI decreased from 26.4 kg/m{superscript 2} to 24.0 kg/m{superscript 2} among women, and from 26.6 kg/m{superscript 2} to 25.2 kg/m{superscript 2} among men. Lower SEP was associated with lower consumption of fruit and vegetables, higher consumption of red and processed meat, and lower VPA in both genders. Women reported healthier diets but less VPA than men. The strongest SEP-BMI mediator among women was VPA (indirect effect: 0.35, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.26, 0.44), followed by fruit and vegetable consumption (0.15, 95% CI 0.08, 0.23) and red and processed meat consumption (0.06, 95% CI 0.02, 0.11). Among men, significant mediators were red and processed meat consumption (0.12, 95% CI 0.03, 0.23), sedentary time (0.11, 95% CI 0.01, 0.24) and VPA (0.10, 95% CI 0.02, 0.21). ConclusionsSocioeconomic inequalities in BMI appear stronger among women and are shaped through partly different mechanisms between genders. Improving VPA may be relevant among low- SEP women, whereas reducing sedentary time may be more relevant among low-SEP men. Reducing red and processed meat is beneficial for both genders.

papers.title: Functional difficulty among children and adolescents aged 5-17 years in Ethiopia: Multilevel analysis of the nationally representative 2024-2025 DHS
papers.abstract: BackgroundPopulation-based data on functional difficulty among school-age children in Ethiopia are scarce. The 2024-2025 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) included, for the first time, the UNICEF/Washington Group Child Functioning Module (CFM) for children aged 5-17 years. We estimated the prevalence and domain distribution of functional difficulty and associated factors in Ethiopia. MethodsWe analysed cross-sectional EDHS data from 11,122 children aged 5-17 years (weighted n = 10,726) and 4,739 mothers. Functional difficulty was defined as "a lot of difficulty" or "cannot do at all" in any of 11 domains, or daily anxiety or depression. We estimated design-based prevalence and fitted multilevel logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) for any, non-affective and affective difficulty. Interviewer effects were examined with random-intercept models and within-cluster comparisons. ResultsOverall, 9.5% (95% CI 8.1-11.1) of children had functional difficulty. Daily depression (6.8%) and anxiety (6.6%) dominated, and 70.3% of affected children had only affective difficulty. Difficulty in at least one non-affective domain affected 2.8% (2.2-3.7), with each domain at 0.5-1.4%. Prevalence ranged from 1.5% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 16.5% in Oromia Regional State. In adjusted models, children not attending school had higher odds of non-affective difficulty (AOR 2.82, 95% CI 2.01-3.96), and girls had lower odds (AOR 0.63, 0.48-0.84). Outcomes clustered strongly within families (sibling correlation 67.7%) and clusters (ICC 20.9%). Six of 163 interviewers (7.9% of the weighted sample) contributed 58.2% of weighted cases of daily anxiety or depression; in the same clusters they recorded daily symptoms for 56.4% of children, against 2.1% for other interviewers. Excluding 11 statistically outlying interviewers reduced the prevalence of any difficulty to 4.6% (3.6-5.8) and of daily anxiety or depression to 3.3%. The associations with school non-attendance and sex were unchanged. ConclusionsFunctional difficulties across the sensory, physical, cognitive, and affective domains, including anxiety or depression, affect about 2-3% of Ethiopian children aged 5-17 years and are strongly associated with being out of school. Appropriate interventions and resource allocation should be considered.
